news_articles_raw.headline: Apple earnings: iPhone prices are 'not immune' to rising memory costs
news_articles_raw.text: Apple (AAPL) stock is stumbling in Thursday's after-hours since reporting fiscal third quarter earnings and revenue that topped estimates, carried by strong iPhone sales. New Street Research technology Infrastructure analyst Antoine Chkaiban explains the problem areas that could emerge down the line for Apple tied to the memory chip shortage. Apple just reported results. Uh the stock at least initially here edging lower in the after hours. Of course, we don't have guidance yet. Antoine, we we would wait for that on the call, but give us your initial reactions on the print. What do you think? Hey Josh, good to see you again. Um, I would say, you know, like the the very strong iPhone 17 cycle that we're experiencing right now, um, was kind of, you know, to be expected. Uh we we were expecting that, you know, you you could see already in US telecom operator um, upgrade rates, you know, stabilizing. Um, the installed base, you know, and refresh dynamics, like stable refresh dynamics, you know, implied that we would see, you know, some units growth and on top of that, as you mentioned, you know, Apple is raising prices. Um, so all of that so far has has um, you know, has has supported Apple's strong results. Now, as you said, um, what we're concerned about uh is that demand destruction, you know, memory driven demand destruction could start hitting the higher end the same way it has already hit, you know, the lower end uh of the market, like cheaper cheaper phones. Um, and so that we'll only know when we hear, you know, uh how Apple is going to guide the next quarter. So that's really what we what we care about. I I'm interested, Antoine, if if Apple raises prices on those next gen iPhones in the fall, you know, is there a price point Antoine where, you know, Tim Cook could raise prices to protect his margins but not meaningfully dent demand? Yes, I mean, smartphones, you know, uh are uh like it's it's an elastic market. There is like a very high elasticity in this market. Consumers are uh sensitive to to prices. They are more sensitive to prices in the lower end. And that's why, you know, so far the higher end has uh, you know, performed better and and you could actually see that also in the past, you know, when you have, you know, like similar, um, like down cycles in the smartphone market, typically the higher end performs better. Uh, but it's not immune. You know, like at the end of the day, uh, when you have memory prices, you know, increasing and know three, four, even 5X, uh, you know, and and um, and memory represents, you know, like even if it's like a single digit percentage of of the phone, you have to raise prices by double digits. Uh, and as you do that, you know, like uh it necessarily impacts your your demand. Uh and so you saw that uh in uh in Qualcomm's print, you saw that in arm's print, you know, and even comments, you know, on uh that that that phenomenon hitting the higher end, um we are concerned that we could start seeing that in Apple's numbers and the guidance.

news_articles_raw.text: Chip stocks are rebounding on Thursday, with the exception of Qualcomm (QCOM), which provided profit guidance that disappointed Wall Street. Quick mention of chips here this morning, which we know have been getting clobbered lately. Um the indications are for as a group for them to be rebounding. Um and there are, you know, some mixed catalysts this morning. You have Samsung on the one hand, um saying that basically they think the chip shortage is going to keep going through 2028. Um and they gave a a a positive outlook. Their net profit was up 1300%. Um of course. Sure. as it does. Um uh operating profit was up 19 times. got Qualcomm on the other hand, give a weak profit forecast. Um, you have arm out there as well. So, but we're seeing a rebound here this morning and there does seem to be, you know, in some of these names and collectively, Qualcomm though is not participating in that. Yeah, and I was just gonna say Qualcomm, I think is a one off. You mean that's because I think they're trying to diversify their revenue stream because they they're losing Apple. Apple used to be 20, 25% of their total revenue and then Apple has started to make their own, you know, um modems, you know, internally and by the end of this year, this should be zero. So they've been, they've known this for years and they're ramping up, but I think that's it's a problem. You know, they're not there yet. And you talked to the CFO yesterday, right? Or today you're going to talk to the CFO. Great. We're uh we'll dive into everything that that happened obviously in the earnings. Uh the smart, I think the smartphone market obviously is, you know, it's a drag on them, right? And it's going to continue to be, they mentioned that, it's just AI means that it's it's interesting that, you know, the same thing with Microsoft too, uh where these companies are diving into AI. I mean, obviously Microsoft's been there, but Qualcomm now has its own rack that's own accelerator, CPU, you know, memory, it's it's all in for the data center. That's all good and great, but then on the back end, it's also hurting you because, you know, all the memory is going to AI, all the storage is going to AI, that means smartphone sales drop, that means for Microsoft, that means Windows PC sales drop. And so, you know, you're you're contending with that. I think Microsoft said that they would see a, a high teens drop in uh Windows uh revenue and and Qualcomm obviously basically just saying the smartphone market is what it is right now. There's we're we're diversifying, automotive will increase, data center will increase, we'll see uh the revenue from that. I forget what it was uh off the top of my head, but there was a certain number by 2029. Um and you know, they're they're basically saying, look, we're doing it, we're we're transitioning away from a heavy dependence on smartphone, but for now, it it it's stinging.

news_articles_raw.headline: Apple and Amazon report rising revenues as investors turn on some tech stocks
news_articles_raw.text: Apple and Amazon both released their second quarter earnings on Thursday, a test of investor confidence in major tech companies amidgrowing concerns over exorbitant AI spending. Apple revealed quarterly revenue of $109.4bn, beating Wall Street expectations of $108.65bn in revenue. It also reported $2.02 earnings per share, driven by sales of its marquee products such as iPhones and laptops. Amazon reported that its revenue was $200.6bn compared with analyst predictions of $196.47bn. The company also grew its AWS cloud computing service and beat market expectations on advertising revenue, thoughfree cash flow declined. Amazon's stock jumped more than 8% in immediate after hours trading. It has been a tough month for several prominent tech companies, with shares in Tesla and Meta both plunging after they revealed huge spending on AI infrastructure in their latest earnings reports. A recent selloff in chip stocks like Nvidia, the result of loss in investor confidence and advances in Chinese chip manufacturing, has also rattled the market. Investors have paid especially close attention in recent weeks to tech companies' free cash flow after large capital expenditures – largely on AI – have caused concern. As the industry continues to plow money into building out AI capabilities in search of future profits, shareholders have become more jittery when earnings reports reveal larger-than expected AI spending. Apple, meanwhile, has benefitted from the chip stock selloff as investors viewed the company as a safe haven amid the broaderAI-driven volatility. The company's stock is up around 23% this year, leading the so-called Magnificent Seven tech stocks, which include Meta, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Tesla and Nvidia. Apple's stock price dropped slightly on Thursday following earnings after it reported its revenue from its services division was below market expectations. Thursday's earnings call was also CEO Tim Cook's final report before he steps down after 15 years as Apple's top executive. Apple's market value grew immensely over Cook's tenure as chief executive, from around $350bn in 2011 tosurpassing the $5tn markdays before Thursday's earnings call. Earlier this month the company overtook Nvidia to become the world's most valuable company. Cook will bereplaced by John Ternus, a longtime hardware engineering executive who has been at the company since 2001. Ternus stated earlier this week that he aims to expand the Apple's entertainment business, which has had success with movies like the blockbuster F1 and streaming series such as The Studio. "As you know, this will be my final earnings call," Cook said on Thursday. "I am beyond excited for John to step into his new role and lead Apple into its next era. He is truly one of a kind and there is no better person to take the helm of the company."

news_articles_raw.headline: Apple Q3 2026 earnings beat estimates but services revenue misses
news_articles_raw.text: Revenue rose 16% to $109.4 billion and EPS climbed 29%, but a shortfall in services sent Apple stock down in after-hours trading © 2026 Quartz Media, Inc. All rights reserved. David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via Getty Images Apple$AAPLreportedits strongest June quarter on record Thursday, with revenue of $109.4 billion up 16% from a year earlier and diluted earnings per share of $2.02 up 29% year over year. Despite beating top-line estimates,Apple's services revenue came in at $30.74 billion, below analyst expectations of $31.22 billion, according toCNBC. The stock fell roughly 3% to 4% in extended trading. Heading into Thursday, the stock had gained about 23% on the year. iPhone revenue of $54.25 billion exceeded estimates of $53.86 billion, representing 22% growth year over year. Mac revenue of $10.35 billion topped an $8.74 billion estimate, but iPad revenue of $6.19 billion fell short of the $6.92 billion analysts had projected. China revenue also disappointed. Sales in Greater China totaled $18.8 billion, well below analyst projections of $19.6 billion, according toBloomberg. Gross margin came in at 50.1%, including a roughly 2% boost from tariff refunds, the company said. Earnings per share also included an $0.11 benefit from tariff refunds. Net income rose to $29.79 billion from $23.43 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. "Today,Appleis proud to report our strongest June quarter ever, with double-digit revenue growth across iPhone, Mac and Services, and in every geographic segment," Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook said in a statement. The quarter is Cook's last as CEO, with the 65-year-oldset to handthe role to hardware engineering chief John Ternus on Sept. 1. Appleis grappling with a worldwide scarcity of memory chips and processors, a crunch that has pushed the company to increase prices on Macs and iPads. Customers have faced lengthening delivery delays on hardware such as the Mac mini and Mac Studio as a result. Applealso recently reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company, overtakingNvidia$NVDAwith a market capitalization of nearly $5 trillion. news_articles_raw.headline: Memecoins Are Trading Against Stocks Now
news_articles_raw.text: Subscribe to Banklessorsign in The main barbell on Robinhood Chain thus far has been memes and real world assets (RWA), and now these trends have coalesced into a new mechanism gaining significant traction on the network:RWA-paired memecoin launches. One of the early pillars on the L2 has beenRobinhood Stock Tokens, e.g. onchain versions of NVDA, SPCX, TSLA, AAPL, etc. Yet to date most memecoins deployed on the chain have been paired againstETH(and specifically WETH) for the widespread liquidity. That said, what would happen if you paired new launches against tokenized stocks instead? We're getting answers in production, as a handful of launchpads are now testing what memecoins' charts look like tied tostocksinstead of ETH. For instance, LONG was anearly oncomerand supports a large swathe of the stock-paired memes dropping on Robinhood Chain. Bankr, havingrecently added this capability, is supporting similar levels of activity here. The popular indie launchpad Pons isadding custom pairsto its V2, and Flaunch isworking on stock tokens, too. So the race is on, but what are the actual mechanics here? Notably, pairing against a stock isn't a pure bet on the meme itself. A pool's price is a ratio, i.e. how much of the stock token it takes to buy one meme token. This dynamic isolates relative demand, but thedollarreturn is that price ratio times whatever the stock itself does over the same stretch. Consider an “XYZ” memecoin launched at a price of 0.001 NVDA. If NVDA is worth $180, each XYZ token starts at $0.18. Enjoying this article? Subscribe to Banklessorsign in Now assume demand for XYZ rises and, one month later, it trades at 0.0015 NVDA. That means XYZ has gained 50% relative to NVDA. Your actual dollar return, however, still depends on what happened to NVDA itself: In other words, buying a stock-paired memecoin is a combined bet: you are betting that the meme will outperform the stock, while also remaining fully exposed to the stock’s price movement. As such, pairing against a stock trades ETH's volatility for the stock's. And since top equities are way less volatile than crypto, the chop amid these pools can be considerably calmer. That's one big appeal of this model. Anotherinteresting dynamic to note here is these sorts of pools let token creators accrue fees in whatever stocks their launches are paired against, meaning they get paid directly with tokenized equity exposure over time (if their pools continue to generate meaningful onchain volume, of course). This sort of architecture mostly depends on liquidity, and Robinhood Stock Tokens don't have tons of that right now. That's straightforward enough to steadily improve going forward, though, and things are apparently liquid enough considering how Robinhood Chainalreadyboasts the most tokenized stock holders in all of crypto. Wow. Less than a month after launch, Robinhood Chain has become the largest network by tokenized stock holders, surpassing Solana, BNB Chain, Ethereum, and Base.Distribution matters.Source:@tokenterminalpic.twitter.com/HIlYA4fjoJ There are geofencing restrictions in place around these tokens in various jurisdictions, so we'll have to see if these soften or tighten in the months ahead. Even in spite of them, this new pool style is already moving serious volume onchain and will lead to further second-order experiments. Keep it on your radar for 2026, as it's a trend poised to continue blooming. Written by William M. Peaster 1024 Articles•View all William M. Business Seasonality and Product Introductions The Company has historically experienced higher net sales in its first quarter compared to other quarters in its fiscal year due in part to seasonal holiday demand. The timing of product introductions can also impact the Company’s net sales to its indirect distribution channels as these channels are filled with new inventory following a product launch, and channel inventory of an older product often declines as the launch of a newer product approaches. The announcement of the initial results of the investigation did not impose any additional tariffs affecting the Company’s products. Separately, on February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling striking down certain tariffs previously imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977. The Company is applying for a refund of tariffs paid, following the processes established by U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Various modifications to U.S. tariffs have been announced, including the imposition of tariffs under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, and further changes could be made in the future, which may include additional measures under the Section 232 semiconductor sector investigation, additional sector-based tariffs, actions under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, or other measures. Tariffs and other measures that are applied to the Company’s products or their components can have a material adverse impact on the Company’s business, results of operations and financial condition, including impacting the Company’s supply chain, the availability of rare earths and other raw materials and components, pricing and gross margin.
